newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S AMP SOCIETY SEES A$2 BLN PROFIT IN '97.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S AMP SOCIETY SEES A$2 BLN PROFIT IN '97.

text.p: The AMP Society, Australia's largest insurance and funds management group, said on Thursday that it expected to achieve profits of about A$2 billion in calendar 1997.
"We do not know what the investment markets will do in the next six months," managing director and chief executive George Trumbull said in a statement.
"Of course, if the investment markets remain as buoyant around the globe as they have been in the first six months, we would expect a higher profit than A$2 billion for the year," Trumbull said.
The AMP plans to list on the Australian Stock Exchange sometime in 1998 and has begun a process of demutualising.
It achieved a profit of A$2.1 billion in calendar 1996, boosted by a one-off payment of A$479 million from Britain's Pearl Group. This compared with a 1995 profit of A$1.9 billion.
Trumbull said AMP had a solid first six months with funds under management rising above A$100 billion for the time.

Total new life premiums rose 36 percent, due mainly to very strong single premium results through the sale of investment and insurance bonds in the United Kingdom and Australia. Annual premium sales continued to fall.
Total premium income was A$3.8 billion in the first half of 1997 and total revenue was A$10.8 billion, AMP said. It did not issue comparative figures.
Investment revenue was nearly A$7 billion. Total group cash low almost doubled to A$1.4 billion due partly to better than expected single premium sales and fewer policy surrenders.

AMP said it achieved strong operations results in Australia from the retail and superannuation areas. In the U.K., Pearl achieved a 58 percent rise in new business with investment bond sales being the main contributor.
